newsitem.title: UK: UK's ITV worried about European curbs on adverts.
newsitem.headline: UK's ITV worried about European curbs on adverts.

text.p: The chairman of Britain's ITV commercial television network on Wednesday urged European legislators not to introduce new curbs on advertising.

"We need legislation which allows room for growth in our market as well as in Europe," ITV chairman Leslie Hill said at a reception for the European Commission and members of the European Parliament held in Brussels.
Hill voiced concern about proposals tabled last week in the European Parliament to limit advertising breaks in films and around children's programmes.
"ITV is Britain's most popular channel with 42 percent of the peaktime audience," said Hill in an excerpt of his text, which was made available in London.
"Our high audience share is in no small part due to our sizeable spend on programmes, amounting to over 800 million pounds in 1997."

"New restrictions on advertising would have a very damaging impact on our ability to invest in original programme production. In turn this would affect the pleasure we give to millions of viewers, reduce employment in our production industry and cut our international sales," he added.
